run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T06:49:27Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is a downstream symptom: from 06:49:27Z the Envoy ingress of frontend-proxy returned HTTP 504 at a steady ~250-270 errors/min, and its access logs show these are 15,000 ms upstream response timeouts on frontend routes (GET /api/products/*, POST /api/checkout, GET /api/recommendations). The route that carries the errors is the product-catalog path: frontend's checkout handler fails with gRPC 13 INTERNAL "failed to prepare order: failed to get product #...", and both frontend and checkout client spans to oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct hang 26-86 s and end with 14 UNAVAILABLE "read: connection reset by peer" / "read ECONNRESET" against the product-catalog Service ClusterIP 100.64.188.136:8080. product-catalog's own GetProduct handler spans are fast (~105-122 us) while its served-call rate collapsed from ~1340 spans/min at 06:47 to 204 at 06:49, 34 at 06:50 and ~0 by 06:55, with ListProducts also reaching 0: callers keep calling, but product-catalog stops completing calls promptly. Its pod stayed Running/ready with 0 restarts, no previous container, no OOM/eviction/failure events, all nodes Ready without pressure, so this is not a crash, eviction or node problem; the container is however configured with an extremely small cpu limit of 15m (memory 30Mi, GOMEMLIMIT 16MiB), uses ~6.9m CPU and is CFS-throttled in ~16-24% of periods, though throttling did not rise at the onset and fell afterwards as traffic collapsed. The specific trigger inside product-catalog (CPU-quota starvation/accept queueing vs a connectivity reset in the service path) is therefore not established.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress error spans rose from 0 to about 250-270 per minute at 06:49:27-06:56:00Z while its non-error ingress span count fell from ~1300-1500/min to ~200-250/min; this is the error signal the RequestErrorRate alert fires on.

frontend-proxy (Envoy) access logs show the failing requests returning '504 UT response_timeout' with 15000/14999 ms durations on GET /api/products/<id>, POST /api/checkout and GET /api/recommendations, while /api/cart and /api/data requests still return 200 via_upstream.

frontend-proxy error spans on operation 'ingress' carry status tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR with duration ~15,000,000 us, and their child span 'router frontend egress' (the call to the frontend service) carries error=true, http.status_code=0 with the same ~15 s duration, i.e. the proxy timed out waiting for the frontend.

frontend has its own error spans in the window: 'POST /api/checkout' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' return http.status_code=500 with exception '13 INTERNAL: failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"0PUK6V6EV0"' (and the same message for other product IDs); frontend's error-rate series attribute the burst to POST /api/checkout and executing api route /api/checkout, not to /api/cart or /api/data.

The checkout service's own server span 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' in trace bc5392e5eae9a2030e73518902a25753 is an error (otel.status_code=ERROR, rpc.grpc.status_code=13) with status description 'failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"0PUK6V6EV0"' after 70.09 s.

checkout's client span 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' in that trace ran 70.01 s and failed with error=true, rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and otel.status_description 'error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer'; 100.64.188.136:8080 is the ClusterIP of the product-catalog Service.

The same pattern appears from other callers: a frontend client span 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' failed after 26.80 s with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: read ECONNRESET', and a checkout client GetProduct span lasted 65.88 s before returning rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

product-catalog's own server spans are fast when they are produced: sampled 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' server spans on service product-catalog have durations of 105-122 us with rpc.grpc.status_code=0, so the handler itself is not slow.

product-catalog's served-call rate collapsed abruptly at the alert onset while request pressure was steady beforehand: GetProduct spans per minute were ~1164-1396 from 06:32 to 06:47, then 878 at 06:48, 204 at 06:49, 34 at 06:50, 10 at 06:51, 134 at 06:52, 32 at 06:53, 2 at 06:54, 0 at 06:55-06:56; ListProducts fell from ~500 per 10 min to 0 by 07:00, and checkout's HTTP POST span rate fell from ~669-1216 per 10 min to 3.7 at 07:05.

product-catalog pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 is a Kubernetes-level healthy object during the incident: phase Running, container ready true, restartCount 0, no previous container instance, started 2026-11-15T06:11:39Z; all 21 pods in otel-demo are Running and ready, and the product-catalog Endpoints object holds one ready address (100.96.4.247:8080) backed by that pod.

No eviction, OOMKilled, restart or failure marks exist for product-catalog: the only events involving it inside the window are Normal 'Updated' events ('Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource'), and all five nodes (including its node i-0b2137ceca968ac10) are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False.

product-catalog runs under an extremely small resource budget: the deployment/container sets limits cpu=15m, memory=30Mi, requests cpu=7m, memory=15Mi, env GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB and PRODUCT_CATALOG_RELOAD_INTERVAL=10; its measured CPU use was ~0.0069 cores before the onset and fell to ~0.0003-0.0011 cores after, with memory working set steady at ~12.0-13.7 MB.

product-catalog's container was already chronically CPU-throttled before the incident and was not throttled harder at the onset: its CFS throttled-periods ratio was 0.16-0.24 from 06:41 to 06:48 and then declined (0.15, 0.15, 0.12, 0.07, 0.06, 0.05); frontend's ratio was 0.19-0.27 before 06:48 and 0.06-0.14 after, and frontend-proxy's throttled-period rate fell from ~0.2-0.5/s to ~0.01-0.07/s over the same interval.

product-catalog's application log output shows normal operation with no error lines: it continuously logs 'Product Found' plus 'Reloading Product Catalog...'/'Loaded 10 products' every ~10 s through the readable period (last readable line 2026-11-15T06:54:40Z), and no line in 06:40-07:05 matched err/error/fail/fatal/panic/timeout/deadline.

The flagd feature-flag configuration in otel-demo has every flag at its default 'off' variant, including productCatalogFailure, paymentFailure, cartFailure and recommendationCacheFailure, so the checked configuration shows no injected application failure.

The synthetic client is also feeling the failure: load-generator spans 'POST' carry error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR with ~15 s durations, and its user_checkout_multi root spans last 45-77 s.

The available resource signals do not show a new CPU-exhaustion event at the onset: product-catalog CPU usage and throttling ratio both fell after 06:48, frontend's throttling ratio fell, frontend-proxy's throttled-period rate fell, all nodes are Ready without pressure and no container restarted, so 'something started consuming more CPU at 06:48' is not supported by these series.

Primary explanation: product-catalog could not accept/serve calls promptly between 06:48 and 06:49 because its container is capped at cpu 15m with chronic CFS throttling, so requests queued ahead of a fast handler - callers then saw 15 s proxy timeouts, 26-86 s client spans and connection resets from the product-catalog ClusterIP, while product-catalog's own handler spans remained ~100 us. The trigger that pushed it over at 06:48 is not shown by the available series.

Alternative hypothesis still open: connection handling to the product-catalog ClusterIP 100.64.188.136:8080 was reset at the service/network path rather than inside the Go handler - the failing spans report 'read: connection reset by peer'/'read ECONNRESET' from that ClusterIP, while the pod stayed ready, its Endpoints entry stayed populated and its handler spans show no errors; this cannot be confirmed without kube-proxy/CNI or product-catalog socket-level data.

Application-level failure injection in product-catalog (for example the flagd productCatalogFailure flag) is rejected for this window: all flagd flags are at the 'off' default, product-catalog logged no error/fail/fatal lines and produced no error spans, and the observed failures are 14 UNAVAILABLE connection resets plus 70 s waits rather than the INTERNAL error such a flag would return from the handler.

frontend or frontend-proxy as the origin of the errors is rejected: their own resource series did not degrade (throttling ratios and throttled-period rates fell after 06:48), frontend-proxy kept serving /api/cart and /api/data with 200 via_upstream during the burst, and every failing route is one that depends on product-catalog (product page, checkout, recommendations).

Impact grouping actually observed: affected with their own failure evidence are frontend-proxy (own 504 ingress spans and 504 access-log lines), frontend (own 500 error spans/exceptions on the checkout route), checkout (own PlaceOrder error span, rpc.grpc.status_code=13) and load-generator (own 504 POST spans). product-catalog shows a collapse in calls it completed and resets reported by its callers, but no error status of its own.

gaps: Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so no deployment/config/image/limit change can be attributed to 06:45-06:50 for product-catalog or any other workload.

The alerting rule named RequestErrorRate returned no_data from list_prometheus_rules, so its exact expression, threshold and evaluation window are unknown; the alert's own 'current: 1.4222' value could not be reproduced from a named series.

No rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count or app_payment_transactions_total series exist in this Prometheus (only otelcol_* matched rpc_/http_/app_), so client-side latency/error SLIs for the checkout->product-catalog and frontend->product-catalog edges are unknown apart from the trace sample.
frontend container logs could not be read (0 lines returned for the 06:45-07:05 window), so frontend-side runtime errors/stack traces beyond span exception fields are unknown.
product-catalog logs are only readable up to 06:54:40Z, so what product-catalog logged after 06:54:40 (including whether it kept serving at a low rate) is unknown.

kube_pod_owner and kube_replicaset_owner series returned no_data, so ownership-chain evidence for a rollout of product-catalog at or before the onset is unavailable; pod startTime 06:11:34-06:11:39 is observed for the product-catalog, frontend and frontend-proxy pods, but whether that reflected a limit/config change could not be verified.
The effective runtime flag values inside the running flagd process were not directly observable; only the mounted flagd-config ConfigMap defaults (all 'off') could be read.
The trace data is a biased sample, so exact rates of product-catalog 14 UNAVAILABLE resets versus long-but-successful calls, and the complete call graph of affected traces, remain unknown.

No CPU-quota, socket, accept-queue or kube-proxy/conntrack data is available to decide between the CPU-starved-accept-path hypothesis and a service-path reset hypothesis, and no NetworkPolicy objects were returned for otel-demo (no_data, not citable).
next_steps: Compare change history around 2026-11-15T06:40-06:50Z for product-catalog (image digest, cpu/memory limits, GOMEMLIMIT, PRODUCT_CATALOG_RELOAD_INTERVAL, flagd flag state) to identify what changed before the collapse.

Capture product-catalog container-level CPU throttling at 15 s resolution plus CPU-quota/accept-queue stats, and profile the gRPC server accept path, to confirm or refute accept-queue starvation under the 15m CPU limit.
Check kube-proxy/conntrack and CNI logs on node i-0b2137ceca968ac10 for resets on the product-catalog Service VIP 100.64.188.136:8080 during 06:48-07:05Z.
Review whether the product-catalog cpu limit of 15m (requests 7m) and memory limit of 30Mi with GOMEMLIMIT 16MiB are appropriate for the observed ~1400 GetProduct spans/min plus 10 s catalog reloads.
Re-check the exact RequestErrorRate rule definition and metric in the rule source, since it is not present in this Prometheus.
